sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:238746
Court No. - 72
Case :- Criminal Misc Anticipatory Bail Application U/S 438 Cr.P.C. No. - 13688 of 2023

Applicant :- Prashant
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Rajeev Tiwari Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Krishan Pahal,J.
1. List has been revised.

2. Heard Sri Anurag Dubey, Advocate holding brief of Sri Rajeev Tiwari, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Arun Kumar, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.
3.

This second anticipatory bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicant in F.I.R./Case Crime No. 261 of 2023, under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471, 171, 120-B of IPC, Police Station Ganga Nagar, District Meerut, with a prayer to enlarge him on anticipatory bail.
His first anticipatory bail application was rejected by this Court vide order dated 08.11.2023 passed in Criminal Misc.
Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No.12385 of 2023.

Prashant vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184863831/
1 4.
Learned counsel for the applicant has stated that his first anticipatory bail application was rejected by this Court only on the ground that the applicant has criminal history of one case.

Learned counsel has placed much reliance on Annexure-3 to the affidavit filed along with anticipatory bail application by which it has been categorically indicated that the applicant has been exonerated in the said case, as such, it has been wrongly stated by learned AGA that he is wanted in it.

Learned counsel for the applicant has also claimed parity with the co-accused Rajat @ Devendra,
who has already been granted anticipatory bail by this Court in Criminal Misc. Anticipatory Bail Application u/s 438 Cr.P.C. No. 12097 of 2023 vide order dated 16.11.2023.
Since the case of the applicant is at par with the co-accused who has already been granted anticipatory bail, the applicant is also entitled for the same on the ground of parity.
5. The prayer for anticipatory bail has been vehemently opposed by learned AGA.
However, the aforesaid factual aspect of the parity to the co-accused has not been disputed by him.

6. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the judgement passed by this Court in Nanha S/o Nabhan Kha vs. State of U.P., 1993 Crl.L.J. 938 and the judgement passed by the Apex Court in Paras Ram Vishnoi vs. The Director,
Central Bureau of Investigation, MANU/SCOR/22410/2021, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the Court is of the view that the applicant is entitled to be granted anticipatory bail in this case.

sentences.text: The bail application is allowed on the ground of parity.
In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the anticipatory bail of the applicant.

9. It is made clear that observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.

(Justice Krishan Pahal) Order Date :- 16.12.2023 Siddhant  Prashant vs State Of U.P. on 16 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/184863831/
